title: Highlights: Franck Balthazar Cornas 2022 Northern Rhône, France
summary: A beautiful low-intervention Cornas. It’s an appellation with just 110 hectares, and in the past people dismissed the wines as
content:
A beautiful low-intervention Cornas. It’s an appellation with just 110 hectares, and in the past people dismissed the wines as rustic. But now this northern Rhône appellation is making some of the planet’s most desired examples of Syrah.

Franck Balthazar Cornas 2022 Northern Rhône, France
13% alcohol. This has beautiful aromatics, with sweet black cherry, some black pepper, a touch of charcoal and some gravelly savouriness. In the mouth there’s some depth, with drying tannins and a bit of grip, but also some grainy, spicy detail. Just a hint of olive with good tannins, and some sleek fruit. Lots of different elements here, but they all pull together in nice harmony, giving a wine that’s really the essence of northern Rhône Syrah, with a clear Cornas accent. Quite brilliant, and so true to type. 95/100

title: Spätburgunder: a deep dive into Germany’s Pinot Noir, with a tasting of 77 wines from top vineyard sites
summary: German wine has been having a good moment for the last decade, and this is one of the wine country
content:
German wine has been having a good moment for the last decade, and this is one of the wine country whose regions have generally benefited from climate chaos and its warming trends. But climate chaos is not a friend you want to be too close too: with the warming trends come extremes, and in many wine regions the best sites might be getting a little too hot in some vintages.

Spätburgunder, Germany’s Pinot Noir, has never been better, and now many regions are making some exciting examples. These notes were taken yesterday in Wiesbaden at the VDP Grosses Gewächs tasting. This is an amazing tasting featuring new single-vineyard wines from the top tier of vineyards in the country, the GGs. All of these wines are from estates who are members of the VDP.

Some explanation is in order. VDP stands for Verband Deutscher Prädikatsweingüter (which translates as the Association of German Prädikat Wine Estates). Fortunately, it’s simply abbreviated as VDP.

There are 198 member producers, and the basis of this wine classification is terroir. Since a revision in 2012, vineyards are classified on four levels:

  • VDP Grosse Lage (equivalent to Grand Cru)
  • VDP Erste Lage (premier cru)
  • VDP Ortswein (village level)
  • VDP Gutswein (regional)

Only the first two tiers are allowed to mention the vineyard name on the label. So a Grosses Gewächs (GG) is a top wine made from a Grosse Lage by a member of the VDP. These wines have to be dry (under 9 g/l residual sugar), and they are the wines we tasted in Wiesbaden. There’s one more layer of complexity: for each region, only certain varieties can make GG wines. If you see GG on a bottle, then you know it is pretty serious, and that it’s made in a dry style (trocken) from a top vineyard site.

The tasting is superbly organized. We sit down, with a list of 400+ wines arranged in flights. You choose which flights you’d like to taste, and the attentive servers bring the wines to your table and pour for you. It makes the whole process of taking notes very straightforward.

These wines are arranged by region, and then site. The GG name is in capitals in each note.

AHR

Deutzerhof Ahrweiler Spätburgunder ECK 2024 Ahr
Nicely structured with a savoury spicy edge to the sweet raspberry and cherry fruit. Some smoky notes. Quite linear and mineral, perhaps showing a bit of oak influence. 93/100          

Meyer-Näkel Ahrweiler Spätburgunder SILBERBERG 2024 Ahr
Smoky and slightly reductive on the nose with vivid berry fruits. The palate is taut and focused but also has lots of flesh. Lovely raspberry and cherry fruit hemmed in nicely by the mineral-like reductive characters. This is an impressive wine. 95/100                                            

Jean Stodden Ahrweiler Spätburgunder ROSENTHAL 2024 Ahr
There’s some nice floral cherry detail here, but also a strong savoury spiciness. It’s fleshy, but also has angles. Fresh and expressive with red cherry and raspberry. Lively, spicy, tapering finish. 94/100     

Deutzerhof Mayschoss Spätburgunder MÖNCHBERG 2024 Ahr
Slightly sweet and sour in character with rich cherry fruit and then some sour cherry and a bit of spicy, tarry framing. Nice balance and poise here. Lovely weight and texture. 93/100

Jean Stodden Rech Spätburgunder HERRENBERG 2024 Ahr
Beautiful elegance and tension here. Some sweet cherry and raspberry fruit with nice flesh, but also some spicy fragility, and a touch of sweet acidity. Just a little haunting sappy greenness too. Stylish. 94/100                                                  

Meyer-Näkel Dernau Spätburgunder PFARRWINGERT 2024 Ahr
Reductive and herby on the nose which seems a bit stinky, but in a nice way. The palate is bold and rich with some green notes as well as really ripe fruit. It’s pushing the edges, but really nice. 94/100                                          

Meyer-Näkel  Walporzheim Spätburgunder KRÄUTERBERG 2024 Ahr
Quite delicate on the nose with some herbs and spice as well as sweet cherry fruit. The palate is sweetly fruited and quite rich with nice mid-palate weight and some lovely herbal detail. 94/100

Deutzerhof Neuenahr Spätburgunder IM KUCKSTEIN 2024 Ahr
A touch of sweet and sour on the nose with bright cherry and plum fruit as well as some prominent acidity, a slight hint of volatility, and then a fresh, long finish. 92/100                                            

Jean Stodden Neuenahr Spätburgunder SONNENBERG 2024 Ahr
Balance and restraint the key here. Some savoury, spicy fringing to the sweet cherry and plum fruit with a slight bitterness on the finish. Has flesh and bones, and potential for development. 94/100                                           

Meyer-Näkel Neuenahr Spätburgunder SONNENBERG 2024 Ahr
Strongly reductive, spicy nose with vibrant raspberry and cherry fruit. The palate has some herbal hints, mineral reductive notes, and brisk acidity on the finish. This is a beautifully complicated wine and I like it. 94/100

SACHSEN

Schloss Proschwitz-Prinz zur Lippe Rottewitz Spätburgunder SCHLOSS PROSCHWITZ 2023 Sachsen
Compact nose with restrained but appealing raspberry and strawberry fruit. The palate has lovely tension with bright red cherry fruit and some wild strawberry, as well as some iodine notes. Really lovely. 94/100                                               

Martin Schwarz Radebeul Spätburgunder FRIEDSTEIN 2022 Sachsen
Pure, elegant floral nose with ethereal red cherries and sappy, leafy notes. The palate is restrained and textural with sweet strawberry fruit and modest tannins. A light, elegant, ethereal style. 95/100

FRANKEN

Rudolf Fürst Klingenberg Spätburgunder SCHLOSSBERG 2024 Franken
Green herbal edge to the vivid berry fruit nose. Compact berry fruits with nice juiciness and focus. Good concentration here, with potential for development. 94/100                                            

Staatlicher Hofkeller Würzburg Grossheubach Spätburgunder BISCHOFSBERG 2024 Franken
Bright, vivid and nicely savoury with a sappy twist to the bold berry fruits. 92/100                                              

Rudolf Fürst Bürgstadt Spätburgunder CENTGRAFENBERG 2024 Franken
Lovely floral aromatics with some sweet raspberry and cherry fruit. The palate is elegant, concentrated and fine, showing some savoury, bloody elements as well as sweet cherry fruit. Nice precision here. 95/100

Rudolf Fürst Bürgstadt Spätburgunder HUNDSRÜCK 2024 Franken
Herbs, blood, undergrowth and iodine join the textured strawberry and cherry fruit here. Shows lovely approachability, but also some seriousness, and all the time elegant. 95/100

Am Stein-Ludwig Knoll Stetten Spätburgunder STEIN 2024 Franken
Some taut herbal notes in the nose here with a plump palate of cherry and berry fruits, with a sour cherry finish. Lots to like here. 93/100                 

RHEINGAU

August Kesseler Assmannshausen Spätburgunder HÖLLENBERG 2024 Rheingau
Wonderful aromatics here. Floral, white pepper, delicate cherries. The palate is fine and expressive, and light but still full flavoured. Exquisite balance and elegance, and lots of joy here. 96/100

August Kesseler Rüdesheim Spätburgunder BERG SCHLOSSBERG 2024 Rheingau
Really nice aromatics, with some floral prettiness as well as spicy savouriness. The palate shows some herbal and spicy complexity, with wild strawberries and red cherries. Such a layered, pretty wine. 96/100

Kaufmann Hattenheim Spätburgunder HASSEL 2024 Rheingau
Sappy and juicy with a sour cherry edge to the bright fruit. Sweet and sour in character but has some nice intensity. Lovely fruit. 92/100                 

Krone Assmannshausen Assmannshausen Spätburgunder HÖLLENBERG 2023 Rheingau
Lovely aromatics with floral cherries and plums. The palate has nice tension and balance with sweet strawberries and cherries, finishing with nice structure. Complex, layered, elegant but structured. 95/100  

RHEINHESSEN                                

J. Neus Ingelheim Spätburgunder PARES 2024 Rheinhessen
Lovely strawberry and cherry fruit here with nice texture. It’s silky and generous with a core of sweet fruit, but there’s enough structure to give balance. Really lovely and nicely complex. 95/100                                        

J. Neus Ingelheim Spätburgunder HORN 2024 Rheinhessen
Distinctive nose has a smoky, spicy edge with some herbs and spice. Savoury detail here with nice weight, but perhaps a bit too much smoky oak influence? 92/100                                                  

Wagner-Stempel Siefersheim Spätburgunder HEERKRETZ 2024 Rheinhessen
Herbal, mulchy nose with some spicy oak. Nice raspberry fruit palate with some more spicy oak adding a frame. 91/100                  

Kühling-Gillot Oppenheim Spätburgunder KREUZ 2024 Rheinhessen
Juicy, bright and vivid with some spicy oak in the mix alongside fresh cherry notes. Sweet fruit core, framed by spice. 91/100                          

Gutzler Westhofen Spätburgunder BRUNNENHÄUSCHEN 2024 Rheinhessen
Juicy, spicy cherries and herbs with some sour cherry and green notes on the finish. Fleshy and juicy. 90/100           

Gutzler Westhofen Spätburgunder MORSTEIN 2024 Rheinhessen     
Supple, light, juicy and vivid with a core of red fruits. Nice sweet fruit core. Simple but tasty. 91/100

Gutzler Gundersheim Spätburgunder HÖLLENBRAND 2024 Rheinhessen
Sweet and sour in character with red cherries, raspberries and some herbs. Nice freshness and juicy intensity here. 92/100          

Battenfeld Spanier Hohen-Sülzen Spätburgunder KIRCHENSTÜCK 2024 Rheinhessen
Sweetly aromatic with some wood spice as well as berry fruits. Nice compact fruit on the palate with a whisky-like edge from the oak. 89/100                 

Battenfeld Spanier Mölsheim Spätburgunder ZELLERWEG AM SCHWARZEN HERRGOTT 2024 Rheinhessen
Some savoury, woody notes on the nose. The palate shows nice focused cherry fruit with a bit of fine spiciness. 91/100   

PFALZ

Philipp Kuhn Laumersheim Spätburgunder STEINBUCKEL 2024 Pfalz
Nice floral aromatics as well as some fresh strawberry and raspberry fruit. Has brightness and energy and also nice fruit. Shows a bit of spicy oak. 91/100                                            

Philipp Kuhn Laumersheim Spätburgunder KIRSCHGARTEN 2024 Pfalz
Herbal hints as well as some spicy woodiness here. Stylish and supple with some raspberry and cherry fruit, with a savoury twist on the finish. 91/100

Odinstal Herxheim Spätburgunder HIMMELREICH 2024 Pfalz
Beautiful warmth on the nose with some mulchy notes as well as sweet strawberry fruit. The palate is bright and vivid with a sour cherry twist to the fruit. This is nicely complex and really alive, made in a distinctive style. 93/100

Rings Leistadt Spätburgunder FELSENBERG 2024 Pfalz
Just beautiful balance here with a core of sweet cherry and berry fruits, supplemented by some well-integrated sweet oak. Good concentration and delivers a lot of pleasure. 94/100           

Rings Kallstadt Spätburgunder SAUMAGEN 2024 Pfalz                 
Supple and bright showing nice fruit purity. There’s some vivid cherry fruit here and a touch of raspberry, and appropriate acidity and structure. 94/100                                             

A. Christmann Königsbach Spätburgunder  IDIG 2024 Pfalz
Floral nose with some sweet and sour character, but it works. Juicy and linear with nice cherry fruit, showing real elegance and poise. Textured and fine. Bright. 94/100                                          

A. Christmann Gimmeldingen Spätburgunder SCHILD 2024 Pfalz
Juicy style with a touch of sweet and sour, showing bright red cherry fruit, finishing with sour cherry. Textured and quite refined, with a bit of structure. Appealing. 93/100                                              

A. Christmann Neustadt Spätburgunder VOGELSANG 2024 Pfalz
Beautifully balanced. Wild strawberry and red cherry with a little spicy bite on the finish, and some good structure. This is juicy on the finish with a degree of elegance. 94/100                                          

Dr. Wehrheim Siebeldingen Spätburgunder IM SONNENSCHEIN 2024 Pfalz               
There’s some elegance to the cherry and strawberry fruit here. Good concentration, some nice texture, and then a spicy bite on the finish. 93/100                 

Bernhart Schweigen Spätburgunder SONNENBERG RG 2024 Pfalz
Some spicy woody notes hover around ethereal red cherry notes on the nose. The palate has nice delicate fruit with a lightness of being, as well as some spicy oak. 92/100  

Jülg Schweigen Spätburgunder SONNENBERG KB 2024 Pfalz
Sappy nose with intense berry fruits as well as some beetroot. Lovely vivid, sweet berry fruits on the palate with a nice acid line and some intriguing mouthfeel. 93/100                                                     

Bernhart Schweigen Spätburgunder SONNENBERG KT 2024 Pfalz
Sappy and ethereal on the nose, but some nice concentration and mid-palate richness in the mouth. Nice detail and focus here. Lovely fruit. 94/100    

Jülg Schweigen Spätburgunder SONNENBERG KT 2024 Pfalz
Sappy cherry fruit on the nose with a hint of beetroot. The palate shows nice concentration and depth with a sour cherry finish. Very stylish and elegant. 95/100                                      

Münzberg-Gunter Keßler Godramstein Spätburgunder MÜNZBERG 2023 Pfalz
Some savoury herbal characters and a bit of structure under sweet cherry and raspberry fruit. Nice balance here with a core of sweet fruit. 93/100

Dr. Wehrheim Birkweiler Spätburgunder KASTANIENBUSCH-KÖPPEL 2023 Pfalz
Supple, rounded and quite elegant with a core of sweet fruit. Lovely wild strawberry and sweet plum, with some structure providing a counter. 94/100                                                 

Friedrich Becker Schweigen Spätburgunder HEYDENREICH 2023 Pfalz
Concentrated, dense berry fruits with good structure and some oak influence. Bold and blocky, but with potential. 92/100             

Friedrich Becker Schweigen Spätburgunder SANKT PAUL 2023 Pfalz
Structured, dense and vivid with lovely berry and cherry fruits, with some firm structure and well integrated oak. Substantial style with potential. 94/100

Friedrich Becker Schweigen Spätburgunder SONNENBERG KB 2023 Pfalz
Juicy and vivid with sour cherries and berries, as well as some oak. A rich, intense style with lots of everything. 92/100                       

Knipser Laumersheim Spätburgunder KIRSCHGARTEN 2022 Pfalz
Compact, classical and rich with sweet berry and cherry fruits as well as some good structure, and a bit of well integrated oak. This is impressive. 94/100

Knipser Grosskarlbach Spätburgunder IM GROSSEN GARTEN 2022 Pfalz
Some wood in the mix here, with a core of sweet cherry and berry fruit. Structured and nicely dense, made in a modern style. 92/100                      

Ökonomierat Rebholz Siebeldingen Spätburgunder IM SONNENSCHEIN 2021 Pfalz
Delicate, leafy, ethereal cherry fruit nose with nice balance. The palate is fine and silky with some sour cherry and plum, showing real elegance. 95/100

BADEN

Bernhard Huber Malterdingen Spätburgunder BIENENBERG 2024 Baden
Focused, fresh vivid nose with bold cherry and berry fruit. The palate shows nice intensity with juicy berries and cherries, a hint of beetroot, and lovely focus. Serious, with potential for development. 96/100                                         

Franz Keller Oberbergen Spätburgunder BASSGEIGE STEINRIESE 2024 Baden
Slightly nervy but intense nose with sour cherries and spice. The palate is vivid, bright, sweetly fruited and finishes slightly bitter, with a spicy layereing. Lots of impact here, and some very nice fruit. But fragile. 94/100                             

Franz Keller Oberrotweil Spätburgunder EICHBERG 2024 Baden
Fleshy, juicy and spicy with a core of sweet berry and cherry fruits, and a touch of sour cherry on the finish. Lively finish. 93/100                 

Franz Keller Achkarren Spätburgunder SCHLOSSBERG 2024 Baden
Juicy, silky strawberry and cherry fruit here with lovely flesh and elegance. There’s some warmth to the fruit. 94/100            

Dr. Heger Achkarren Spätburgunder SCHLOSSBERG 2024 Baden
Supple and fresh with some warmth to the cherry and strawberry fruit. Elegant texture here: it’s friendly and approachable, but there’s some fine spicy framing. 93/100                                           

Dr. Heger Ihringen Spätburgunder WINKLERBERG WINKLEN 2024 Baden
Warm, ethereal nose with a bit of spice and ripe cherry and strawberry fruit. The palate is fresh and supple with nice sweet red fruits and good acidity. A lovely lighter, more elegant style. 94/100  

Dr. Heger Ihringen Spätburgunder WINKLERBERG WANNE 2024 Baden
Beautifully focused in a lighter style but still with plenty of flavour. Textured red cherry fruit with some nice fine spicy detail. This shows lovely balance and weight. 95/100                                      

Dr. Heger Ihringen Spätburgunder VORDERER WINKLERBERG 2024 Baden
A lighter style with elegant, ethereal red cherry and wild strawberry fruit, showing nice balance and tension as well as textured fruit. 94/100                 

Bercher Burkheim Spätburgunder FEUERBERG KESSELBERG 2023 Baden
Slightly rubbery, leathery notes on the nose, then some savoury detail to the berry fruits on the palate. Something isn’t quite right here, but there’s nice fruit. 88/100                                             

Salwey Oberrotweil Spätburgunder EICHBERG 2023 Baden
Silky, spicy cherry and berry fruits here with a savoury, slightly woody edge on the palate. Nice fruit density and some appeal. 92/100

Salwey Oberrotweil Spätburgunder KIRCHBERG 2023 Baden
This has a core of sweet cherry and berry fruit, complemented on the palate by some spicy, woody notes. Good intensity of flavour. Finishes grippy. 90/100

Blankenhorn Schliengen Spätburgunder SONNENSTÜCK 2023 Baden
Bright, compact cherry and berry fruits with some firm tannin. Quite extractive with a slightly drying finish. But nice fruit. 90/100                                                    

Heitlinger Odenheim Spätburgunder KÖNIGSBECHER 2022 Baden
Warm aromatics with a hint of almond. Sweet, ripe strawberry and cherry fruit here with good density. Very stylish and compact. 94/100                                   

Burg Ravensburg Sulzfeld Spätburgunder LÖCHLE 2022 Baden
Sweet fruit core with cherries and berries. Nice silkiness with a slightly savoury twist to the fruit. Very stylish and balanced. 94/100

Lämmlin-Schindler Mauchen Spätburgunder FRAUENBERG 2022 Baden
Bright and slightly edgy with a liqueur-like edge to the raspberry and cherry fruit, and then some tartness on the finish. Very likeable. 93/100                                   

Staatsweingut Freiburg Blankenhornsberg Spätburgunder DOKTORGARTEN WINKLEN 2021 Baden
Some soft, sweet strawberry fruit here along with some nice cherry and plum fruit. Nice finesse. Easy and tasty. 92/100  

WÜRTTEMBERG                              

Rainer Schnaitmann Fellbach Spätburgunder LÄMMLER 2024 Württemberg             
Haunting nose with some sappy green hints and sweet berry fruits. The palate is grainy with nice grip, and some lovely detail. Good weight and structure with a nice wet stone finish. 94/100                                   

Aldinger Fellbach Spätburgunder LÄMMLER KAISER 2024 Württemberg
Slightly reductive edge to the red berry fruits on the nose. The palate is juicy and crunchy with raspberry and cherry, showing nice focus and presence. Edgy wine, but nice. 93/100

Aldinger Untertürkheim Spätburgunder GIPS MARIENGLAS® 2024 Württemberg
Smoky, reductive edge to the nose which shows spicy berry fruits. The palate is linear, focused and detailed, and the reduction works well, framing the vivid raspberry and black cherry fruit. Nice precision. 95/100                              

Wöhrwag Stuttgart Spätburgunder HERZOGENBERG 2024 Württemberg
Sappy, florakl, slightly musky nose with sweet strawberry fruit. The palate has lovely smooth, sliky fruit with ripeness and elegance, and a slight spicy framing. Delicious in this lighter style. 94/100

Graf Neipperg Neipperg Spätburgunder SCHLOSSBERG 2024 Württemberg
Fruity, bright and showing lovely balance. There’s sweet fruit here – cherries and ripe plums – but also nice freshness and detail. So expressive. 94/100

Staatsweingut Weinsberg Gundelsheim Spätburgunder HIMMELREICH 2024 Württemberg
Wood spice and berry fruits on the nose. A little bit of volatile acidity, too. Some nice fruit, but it’s a bit disjointed. 88/100

Beurer Stetten Spätburgunder MÖNCHBERG ÖDE HALDE 2023 Württemberg
Juicy, tart and lively with red cherry and berry fruits, finishing with some sour cherry. 91/100

Dautel Oberstenfeld Spätburgunder FORSTBERG 2023 Württemberg
Nice density of silky cherry and berry fruits. Forward and fruity with good energy and a sour cherry twist on the finish. 93/100      

Dautel Bönnigheim Spätburgunder SCHUPEN 2023 Württemberg
Supple and textural with nice sweet fruit. Wild strawberries and cherries with some plummy detail. Silky and textural with nice finesse. 94/100

Graf Neipperg Schwaigern Spätburgunder RUTHE 2023 Württemberg
Silky, elegant and ethereal with some subtle herbiness and a touch of sweet cherry, finishing with nice brightness. Very stylish. 94/100

title: Gallery: in the vineyards of the Ahr Valley, Germany
summary: I arrived in the Ahr Valley this afternoon and took a walk around the vineyards. This is a Pinot Noir
content: I arrived in the Ahr Valley this afternoon and took a walk around the vineyards. This is a Pinot Noir specialist region, and I think most of the grapes pictured here are Pinot Noir, but some could also be Fruhburgunder. There’s a wide variation in cropping levels and ripening stage. Soils here are schist, and some of the vineyards are very steep. They are all on hills.

title: Exploring the Hunter Valley (3) Margan
summary: Website: https://www.margan.com.au/ Margan is an important Hunter Valley producer making some very interesting wines, and championing newer varieties that show
content:
Website: https://www.margan.com.au/

Margan is an important Hunter Valley producer making some very interesting wines, and championing newer varieties that show a lot of promise.

The story. Andrew Margan left Tyrrells and, with his wife Lisa, decided to build his own vineyard in a Hunter GI called Broke Fordwich. With 3 young kids to support, he says he went a bit too commercial, and built a 30 000 case wine brand. This has now been pulled back a bit, focusing on quality with a single block focus, pulling out some of the entry-level stuff. This year they pulled out 40 acres of vines, mostly Verdelho, which Andrew says just isn’t aspirational for them.

He’s now been joined by the next generation, his son Ollie, who is fully involved. The Margan winemaker is Giacomo Soldani.

The home vineyard is 40 acres, including significant plantings of Barbera (9 acres) and Albariño (14 acres with a plan to plant 6 more). They also have a second site, Fordwich Hill, which is a large 120 acre vineyard planted by Lindemans in 1974.

Pushed by Ollie, Andrew has started farming the home block regeneratively. Initially they lost some yield, going down from 50 tons to 20, but this has now bounced back to around 30. But the quality has been enhanced. Ollie says that they are now seeing more site differences with the same variety.

The Fordwich Hill site has soils rich in dolorite, which is volcanic rock formed without oxygen (basalt is formed with oxygen). They are red in colour, and are quite consistent, with the variable being the amount of gravel in the top soil (larger fragments of dolorite). The home vineyard has plugs of volcanic soil, but also sandy soils from a creek that’s near here. The hillside plots of grey clay on sandstone.

We tasted some barrel/tank samples from 2026. Andrew says that this was a vintage with a ridiculously short hang time but the wines have amazing depth of flavour and tannic structure.

Chardonnay 2026 This is clone p58 from the home vineyard. Stony, mineral, finely spiced with lovely weight and texture. Good balance.

Chardonnay 2026 This is Timbervines Fordwich, with red soils. Bernard clones. Lively, bright and vivid with good acidity. Mealy, nutty and showing a fine spicy edge.

Shiraz 2026 From Fordwich. 40 days on skins in large oak. Wonderful purity: supple, bright, linear, refined and elegant in style.

Shiraz 2026 Fordwich Hill, a gully that attracts cooler air. Bright and vivid with nice density. Floral with some nice spice. Lovely purity and finesse.

Cabernet Sauvignon 2026 From Fordwich, aged in concrete with extended time on skins. Lovely leafy blackcurrant fruit on the nose with some chalkiness. Elegant and structured with a hint of coffee bean.

Albarino 2026 This is the Breaking Ground version and there are two picks. The riper pick has 12 days on skins, the other pick is stainless steel. Combined into concrete. This is really aromatic with lovely intensity. Vivid, rich and textured. Really interesting.

Barbera 2026 Lovely weight and volume with a nice salty edge to the ripe, sweet cherry and berry fruits.

Mourvèdre 2026 This is Saxonvale. Juicy, linear, bright and showing redcurrant and raspberry fruit. Some spicy definition and good structure.

Finished wines

Margan Ceres Hill Albariño 2026 Hunter Valley, Australia
Whole bunch pressed and then fermented and aged in stainless steel. This is pure, saline and crystalline with juicy citrus and pear fruit, as well as a touch of apricot. Nice precision. 93/100

Margan Breaking Ground Albariño 2025 Hunter Valley, Australia
Half skin fermented, half whole-bunch pressed. Beautiful aromatics: floral with some peach and apricot. The palate is energetic and saline with nice acidity and a bit of structure. So delicious, showing real complexity, but still varietally true. 94/100

Margan Aged Release Semillon 2013 Hunter Valley, Australia
This is from the red coils. Utterly classic with some toast and honey, as well as a touch of creaminess under the bright citrus fruit. There’s a touch of lime oil. This is quite beautiful, and it’s still so primary. 93/100

Margan Ceres Hill Chardonnay 2025 Hunter Valley, Australia
Bright, saline and expressive with lovely citrus and pear fruit, showing nice volume and purity. Very expressive. 93/100

Margan Timbervines Chardonnay 2025 Hunter Valley, Australia
This has concentration, with appealing spice-laden peach and pear fruit, showing some salinity and nice tension. Finely spiced. So expressive and vivid. 94/100

Margan MC4 Shiraz 2024 Hunter Valley, Australia
This is raised in concrete. Supple and elegant with a nice stony edge to the raspberry and cherry fruit. Really expressive with nice balance. 93/100

Margan Saxonvale Mourvèdre 2025 Hunter Valley, Australia
Sappy with a slight green edge to the nose. Juicy and slightly stony, showing elegant raspberry and cherry fruit. Grainy with a bit of tannin. Some rose petal notes. Very pretty. 94/100

Margan Shiraz 2007 Hunter Valley, Australia
Savoury and spicy with nice definition, and notes of pepper and earth. Grippy and grainy with nice evolution. 92/100

Margan Botrytis Semillon 2024 Hunter Valley, Australia
9.5% alcohol. This is fresh and supple with lovely pear and peach notes, as well as citrus, and a bit of spicy detail. Hints of tea, too. 94/100

title: Exploring the Hunter Valley (2) judging the Hunter Valley Wine Show
summary: Tell your friends that you’ve just been in the Hunter Valley judging 80 wines a day with nice people, they’ll
content:
Tell your friends that you’ve just been in the Hunter Valley judging 80 wines a day with nice people, they’ll probably say you’ve been on holiday. Let me tell you: judging a wine show is hard work. Rewarding, interesting and educational, for sure, but proper hard work.

This year I was asked to be the overseas judge for the Hunter Valley Wine Show. In Australia the show system is an important part of the wine ecosystem, and winemakers are very keen to be show judges. But it’s a long way to the top. Typically, prospective judges will do the Australian Wine Research Institute AWAC (Advance Wine Assessment Course), and then spend time working as wine show stewards, and then apprentices before they land a judging position. So it’s a big deal to be asked to be an overseas judge and take up one of those precious slots.

The Hunter show is one of the regional shows. There are also national shows, judging wines from across the country. I really like the idea of regional shows. As a judge, you get a deep dive into the region, tasting so many different wines next to each other. And then the fact that you are in the region means there is a chance to meet with winemakers, visit a few wineries, and generally get under the skin of the region aside from the judging process itself.

This was the 54th edition of the Hunter show, and over 650 wines were entered from 69 producers.

Day 1

So, day 1. The first flight of the day was 21 Chardonnays from the 2024 vintage. This was pretty solid, and I awarded one gold, 7 slivers and 11 bronzes (but I was one of three judges and two associates on the panel, so each of our scores is just the starting point of the discussion). Many of the wines showed lovely fruit purity coupled with good acidity. There weren’t any big oak monsters: overall the oak use was really well managed. What happens with this judging process is that our scores and notes are entered into the system, then when everyone has finished judging we can see all the scores and notes for each wine, which helps us then discuss them, where this is needed.

The panel chair then decides which wines to call back, and these are randomized and referred to by letter rather than number, so we are effectively judging them afresh. Also, it stops people from being attached to ‘their’ gold. Anything with significant support (one or two golds, and then some high silvers) is likely to be called back so we can have another look. From this set of five or six wines (occasionally more for a strong category), we decide on the golds. And the competition chair comes and looks at these wines too: this helps with consistency, because they look at all the wines that have been called back from the three panels. And for big flights, they might be shared among two or three panels, so this benchmarking is needed.

The second flight was quite a challenge: 23 Semillons from the 2025 vintage. It’s hard tasting these wines so young, but after a bit of discussion we found 4 golds from this, including one standout wine. I just don’t have experience with Hunter Semillon this young, so this was a learning experience.

Then we had 2025 Chardonnay. I liked some of these wines a lot, giving 3 golds and 5 silvers, as well as quite a few bronzes. Some of them were presumably more commercial, lower-priced offerings. But the best were quite thrilling. This took us through to a rather late lunch, at 1430.

The afternoon session: time for the star turn: 24 aged Hunter Semillons from 2018 back to 2006. I gave seven golds. This is a remarkable category to judge, because of the quality of the wines entered, and the uniqueness of this style. It was clear that the evolution of many of these wines is glacially slow.

Because there were so many potential golds here, there was no call back: instead we went back to the flight we’d already judged and pulled back around half the wines, looking at them in more detail. The merits of the older wines are a little clearer than with the young wines, so there were a closer agreement among the judges.

Day 2

Day 2 began with some more Semillon action, in the form of 24 wines from the 2026 vintage. These were just babies, and this makes judging tricky: this distinctive linear, high-acid style of wine very early in its life is difficult to assess. But that’s why we have panels. I gave no golds but dished out a few high silvers, and then when we did a call back of 6 wines, I gave two golds. The overall result from the panel was three golds, although there was quite a bit of variation in the panel for all but one, which got a full house of 95 point scores.

This was followed with the first reds I’d seen in the competition. A set of 18 Shiraz wines from 2024, which for many producers is current release. There was quite a diversity of styles, but we managed to identify four gold-medal-winning wines here. One was quite dense and rich, another elegant and nervous, another mid-weight and complex – you get the idea. It’s hard to put Hunter Shiraz in a box: there is a much broader palette of wine styles than with Semillon, which is a much more defined style. But the best Hunter Shiraz wines are really nice, and quite different to South Australian examples.

After lunch, back to Semillon, with more aged examples. This time it wasn’t a library class, but a more general class (there must be 50 dozen wines, whereas for the library category you don’t need to have so many bottles available).

Day 3

Day 3 involved three tasks. First of all I was asked to help judge the Provenance Class, which is where producers enter three different vintages of the same wine. We had quite a lot of Semillons, and a shorter list of Shiraz wines. This is an interesting exercise, and in the end the five of us (three panel chairs, the chair of show and me) managed to agree on one of each, and then decided to give the overall award to the Semillon.

And then in the afternoon, trophy judging. This is quite fun, seeing which wines have come through. Some of the decisions are already made by the competition chair and the panel chairs, who look through the golds for each category. But then all the judges are involved in the next level of trophy judging. For example, there has to be an overall red, an overall white, a Chardonnay, a Semillon and so on. So this process is quite exciting.

Finally, all the judging was done and the paperwork was signed, and I went round the back where I was free to try any of the wines entered into the competition. My specific job was to find the ‘silver bullet’ winner, which is a wine that might not have done well in the competition, and isn’t one of the star categories that are already well rewarded (Semillon, Shiraz and Chardonnay). So I tasted through a bunch of what might be called alternative varieties. There were some lovely wines and I came up with a shortlist of three: a partial skin-ferment Albariño, a Chenin Blanc and a Nero d’Avola. The Nero d’Avola was my final choice.

Day 4

In the morning: the exhibitors tasting. All the wines entered were lined up, with an indication as to the result they got (but no trophy announcements). Those who exhibited were able to come and taste through. I joined in and tasted a bunch more wines, sighted this time. This was a very useful exercise.

Then in the afternoon, competition chair Toni Paterson and I went on some vineyard visits, looking at some of the regions most revered sites.

Day 5

One thing remained: the awards lunch, which is a big deal in the region. Everyone gets dressed up, pretty much the whole Hunter wine community attends, and there’s a great lunch with gold-medal wines on the table, and an announcement of all the trophies. It was a lovely time. I had to give a short speech, as did Toni. It’s just so great to see everyone thrilled to be recognized in this way, and the trophies were nicely spread around this year.

title: Exploring the Hunter Valley, Australia’s oldest wine region (1) introduction
summary: It was almost 200 years ago, in 1828, when the Hunter Valley became a wine region. It’s the oldest in
content:
It was almost 200 years ago, in 1828, when the Hunter Valley became a wine region. It’s the oldest in Australia, and for a while in the 19th century it was the largest. Now, it’s small, boutique and has a distinctive personality.

Despite the hot, humid climate this has been the source of some of the country’s leading wines, and long-term Hunter resident Maurice O’Shea was one of the most revered of all Australian winemakers, fashioning some astonishing red table wines in an era when the industry focus was largely on fortifieds.

And Hunter Valley Semillon is one of Australia’s iconic wine styles, made in a crisp, lean tight style that then morphs with many years in bottle into something that’s toasty and intricate.

Located just 160 km (2 hours’ drive) from Sydney, the Hunter thrived in part because of this proximity to a major city, and is now an important tourism destination.

Many of the early pioneers such as Lindemans and Wyndham are still important names in the Australian wine scene, and then later the likes of Tyrrell’s and McWilliams  helped grow the reputation of the region. And in Maurice O’Shea, who established Mount Pleasant in 1921, and went on to make some of Australia’s most sought-after wines that aged beautifully we have one of the country’s true wine legends.

There are now 2600 hectares of vines here with 150 wineries, so it is a small region, and of late more vines have been removed than have been planted. But some of the vineyards that have been uprooted were suboptimal. The real challenge is in making sure that the good old vineyards (and the Hunter has lots of these) stay in the ground in the face of rising real estate values.

The region, which is found in the foothills of the Brokeback Range, is split into the Lower Hunter, around Pokolbin, and the Upper Hunter. The Lower Hunter is where most of the region’s well known wineries are located.

The surprise ticket from the Hunter is its Semillon, which is a unique style. It’s not a variety that you’d expect to do well in a warm-climate region such as this, but it has grown to become a unique style. The grapes are picked quite early with relatively low potential alcohol, at around 11 per cent. They are fermented in stainless steel to yield a fairly tart, bright, slightly neutral white wine. But then time in bottle transforms this into a complex wine with toast, lanolin and spice aromas, as well as zippy citrus fruit. It ages fabulously, and the switch to screwcap from cork has enhanced the consistency of this ageing: in the past, there was too much variation and even failure because of the closure.

And Shiraz also excels: Brokenwood’s Graveyard Hermitage (now renamed Shiraz) has long been a classic that has great ageing potential. Aside from Semillon, the Hunter has also been an important part of the Australian Chardonnay story, with Tyrrell’s Vat 47 making a strong claim to being Australia’s first commercial Chardonnay bottling back in 1971. Their HVD vineyard, planted in 1908, has some of the world’s oldest Chardonnay vines.

Semillon is the dominant variety in the Hunter, making up just over 30 per cent of plantings. Next up is Shiraz, the ever-adaptable variety that does so well here too. And Chardonnay makes up the third of the region’s viticultural specialities, capable of turning out complex and sometimes ageworthy examples. There are a range of other varieties found here, notably Verdelho, which makes crisp, focused whites, and makes up 14 per cent of plantings here.

Alternative varieties are looking interesting. The front runner is probably Albariño, which does well here. Fiano shows promise; Pecorino may ripen a little too fast. I tasted a really good Nero d’Avola, and an interesting Sangiovese. Can we include Pinot Noir here? It has been present in the Hunter for a long time, and forms half of a very interesting historic blend with Shiraz. But it’s also doing quite well on its own.

I spent just under a week in the region in August 2026, during which I judged the Hunter Valley Wine Show. And I came away enthused.

title: Highlights: Sandridge Barton Don’t Feed The Ponies Billy Light Red 2025 Devon, England

content:
Website: https://shop.sandridgebarton.com/products/dont-feed-the-ponies-billy-2025

Sandridge Barton Don’t Feed The Ponies Billy Light Red 2025 Devon, England
10.6% alcohol. Pinot Noir, Pinot Precocé, Pinot Gris and Bacchus. Pink/red in colour, this is a delicious lighter red that’s best served chilled. So fresh and juicy with raspberry, cranberry and some lemony brightness. This really is the meeting point of red and white wine, with red wine aromas and a white wine mouthfeel. There’s a little bit of carbon dioxide that adds some more freshness. Just deliciously drinkable with a lovely energy. 91/100 (£23 direct from Sandridge Barton)

title: Four wines from Virginia in the USA
summary: I tried these four wines from Virginia in the USA. It’s a state that is quite challenging for viticulture, with
content:
I tried these four wines from Virginia in the USA. It’s a state that is quite challenging for viticulture, with hot humid summers. But the quality is there, if these four bottles are anything to go by. There are 300 wineries and 1600 hectares of vineyards, with 75% Vitis vinifera and 25% hybrids. This is a significant presence. I liked these four wines quite a bit.

Website: https://rosemontofvirginia.com/

Rosemont of Virginia Kilravock 2023 Virginia, USA
14.3% alcohol. 44% Merlot, 28% Cabernet Franc, 28% Petit Verdot, aged for 18 months in a mix of French oak and a bit of American). This is such a smooth and harmonious wine with sweet cherries and berries, some floral notes, and well resolved tannins. Smooth, elegant and expressive with lovely purity and finesse. Red cherries, plums, and even some sweet strawberry. There’s such an ease to this wine, but also a bit of spicy, tannic bite (but not too much) framing the sweet fruit well. This is really good, and it’s really pretty. 93/100

Website: https://shop.smvwines.com/

Southwest Mountains Vineyards SMV Merlot 2023 Monticello, Virginia, USA
This is beautifully elegant, with smooth, soft black cherry and blackberry fruit with very soft tannins and an ease on the palate. Nice concentration with nice texture and a core of very sweet strawberry and cherry fruit. It’s pure with a core of sweet, smooth fruit, with just enough tannin to hold it together. It’s so nice, in this ripe, smooth, balanced red wine space. 93/100

Website: https://www.bbvwine.com/

Barboursville Cabernet Franc Reserve 2023 Virginia, USA
10% Petit Verdot in the blend. This is smooth, floral, silky and elegant with mellow blackcurrant and berry fruit. There’s a lovely purity and texture to this wine, and it is deeply satisfying and smooth. Such purity, with fi2e-grained chalky texture under the fruit. This is a really beautiful expression of Cabernet Franc showing ease and elegance. Such harmony, and amazing value at $25 in the USA. 92/100


Website: https://www.domainefinotva.com/

Domaine Finot Turk Mountain Vineyards Petit Verdot 2023 Montecillo, Virginia
12.5% alcohol. Whole cluster fermentation with wild yeasts. No added sulfites. There’s a spicy, savoury framing to the nose with sweet cherry and berry fruits. The palate is quite structured with drying tannins under the sweet berry and black fruits. There’s a lovely balance to this wine. The no-added-sulfites has made the tannins stick out a tiny bit – the immense phenolic strength of this wine protects it from oxygen, but at the costs of the tannins going quite dry. But it’s really voluminous, delicious and gastronomic. I have no idea where I’d place this if I tasted it blind: the fruit is ripe and sweet, but then there’s this grainy, grippy structure. I really like it. 93/100 [Note added later: on day 2, this had started to show signs of mousiness, so open it and drink it in one sitting!]

title: Restaurants: Dear Sainte Éloise, Sydney, with three nice wines
summary: Website: https://www.lovetillygroup.com/dear-sainte-eloise After an afternoon walking around Sydney, I popped into Dear Saint Éloise, which is a wine-focused casual restaurant
content:
Website: https://www.lovetillygroup.com/dear-sainte-eloise

After an afternoon walking around Sydney, I popped into Dear Saint Éloise, which is a wine-focused casual restaurant in Potts Point. The space is really relaxed, and I walked in without a booking and sat at the bar.

The wine list is quite brilliant, with a focus on low-intervention wines, although I wouldn’t say this is a ‘natural’ list, even though a lot of wines fall into the natural bracket. And I really like that it’s got strong Australian representation, as well as European. I couldn’t stretch to a bottle, but I did order three wines by the glass, all Australian, and all interesting.

And the food is excellent. All three dishes I ordered were beautifully presented, and also had great flavour.

Fleet Lichen Pinot Noir 2025 Gippsland, Australia
Gippsland is a really interesting Victorian subregion with a cool climate. This Pinot Noir comes from Leongatha in South Gippsland, with deep clay loams rich in basalt. The vineyard was planted in 1990 on its own roots, and the clones are 115, D5V12 and 777. This is bright and tart with lovely sleek cherry fruit. Refreshing with some brisk acid holding things together. Lovely juicy energy and purity here. I love the vibrancy and depth of flavour. 93/100

Domaine Simha Sanskrit Gamay 2025 Tasmania, Australia
12% alcohol. From the Derwent Valley in Tasmania, this is from a single vineyard. Whole bunch wild ferment, traditional pigeage, matured for 6 months in a seasoned demi muid. Basket pressed, then bottled unfined and unfiltered. This is delicious. Sappy and bright with a nice green edge to the fluid, silky berry fruits. Such purity and poise. There’s also a bit of chalky structure here. Beautiful Gamay. 94/100

Sabi Wabi Nomu Syrah 2025 Hunter Valley, Australia 
This is made from two parcels in Pokolbin. One was direct pressed and fermented in a used barrel. The other was whole berry fermented, then pressed to stainless steel. The fact that one parcel was fermented off the skins makes a lighter red with low tannin. Designed to be served chilled this has lovely texture with soft tannins, and sweet cherry and strawberry fruit. It’s deliciously ripe and smooth but there’s still just a hint of peppery detail. Lovely weight here. 92/100

title: Cas ‘Amaro, a growing wine tourism and winemaking project in several Portuguese regions
summary: Website: https://www.casamaro.pt/en/index.php Cas ‘Amaro is an emerging winemaking and wine tourism powerhouse. They began in 2016 with the acquisition of
content:
Website: https://www.casamaro.pt/en/index.php

Cas ‘Amaro is an emerging winemaking and wine tourism powerhouse. They began in 2016 with the acquisition of an estate in Alenquer, in the Lisboa region. This old winery had 4.5 hectares of vineyards. They redeveloped it into luxury accommodation and since 2022 have been making wines here from organically farmed grapes.

But they have also bought properties in other Portuguese wine regions, and these are also earmarked for conversion into high-end wine tourism ventures. In the Alentejo they bought Herdade Monte de Castelete, a 70 hectare property. In the Douro they have 30 hectares of vineyard in the Cima Corgo after acquiring São Joaquim and Navarro, and they have the 25 hectare Quinto do Busto in Vinho Verde. Finally, there’s Quinta da Fontalta in the Dão.

I tasted these wines with Ricardo Santos, who is part-time winemaking director here. His own project is XXVI Talhas in the Alentejo.

Cas ‘Amaro Sercial Pét Nat 2024 Lisboa, Portugal
This has no sulfites added, and it isn’t disgorged. Cloudy and lively with bright grapefruit, pear and lime fruitiness. This is tangy and lively, and it’s quite lovely. 92/100

Madame Pió Sercial Branca Reserva 2024 Lisboa, Portugal
6 months in oak. Mineral, spicy and fresh with high acidity and some nice subtle oak influence. Nice intensity. 90/100

Madame Pió Arinto Reserva 2021 Lisboa, Portugal
Lovely weight here with good acidity. Pure and stony with nice citrus drive. Quite mineral. Lovely. 92/100

Mitologia Encruzado 2023 Dão, Portugal
Lively, stony and elegant, with nice pure citrus fruit. This has great presence with good acidity. Linear. 93/100

Falatório Rosé 2023 Lisboa, Portugal
Tinta Miuda and Camarate. Pale pink in colour. Lovely citrus, apple and cherry fruit with some pear. A dry style with nice presence and good acidity. 91/100

Falatório Bastardo 2022 Lisboa, Portugal
12.5% alcohol. Raised in concrete tanks. Lighter-style red that’s soft with nice stony, herby detail to the cherry and ripe strawberry fruit. Elegant style. 93/100

Implause Tinto Field Blend 2023 Alentejo, Portugal
13% alcohol. From Estremoz. Stainless steel. Juicy, bright and vivid with red cherry and raspberry fruit. Very pure and enticing. Supple and stony with lovely detail. 93/100

Caminho Jaen 2023 Dão, Portugal
Stainless steel. Juicy and crunchy with bright fruit but also some harmony. Fresh and pure with lovely fruit. Expressive. 93/100

Madame Pió Castelão 2022 Lisboa, Portugal
12.5% alcohol. Lovely red cherry fruit with nice crunch. Bright and expressive with some raspberry. Showing great focus and concentration. Serious. 94/100

Madame Pió Tinta Miuda 2021 Lisboa, Portugal
Slightly appley nose. Tannic and fresh and bright with bold cherry and raspberry fruit, Nice density, but there’s a hint of oxidative character here on the fringes. 90/100
